findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — [P1 confidence=100] `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` When an attendee or team manager exercises this allowed mutation for another organizer’s booking, the calendar update is executed with the caller’s integration credentials instead of the booking owner’s credentials, so the persisted guest set and the organizer-owned external event diverge.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — [P1 confidence=100] `const bookingAttendees = await prisma.booking.update({` When the subsequent external calendar update rejects, the database commit has already made the guest an attendee and the same request cannot repair the external event because the prefilter now rejects that guest as already present.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — [P1 confidence=100] `guests: z.array(z.string().email()),` A caller can submit an arbitrarily large guest set that is fully materialized, inserted, translated, propagated to the calendar provider, and fanned out through one concurrent email promise per attendee, creating unbounded work and outbound concurrency in a single mutation.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — [P1 confidence=100] `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email) &&` When the input repeats a new address or varies only its case, each copy passes this comparison against only the old snapshot and creates multiple attendee identities and duplicate downstream invitations for the same mailbox.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:529 — [P2 confidence=100] `emailsToSend.push(sendEmail(() => new OrganizerAddGuestsEmail({ calEvent: calendarEvent })));` When the event type disables standard host or attendee emails, this unconditional guest-notification pipeline bypasses the shared event-type email policy and sends messages that the booking configuration declares disabled.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:147 — [P2 confidence=100] `};` When a team booking adds a guest, this reconstructed `CalendarEvent` omits `team`, making the email manager’s `calendarEvent.team?.members` integration branch unreachable and leaving the other assigned hosts outside the update contract.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — [P2 confidence=100] `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` When one request mixes an existing attendee with a genuinely new guest, passing the raw command instead of the accepted `uniqueGuests` result makes the email layer treat the existing attendee as newly added and send a fresh scheduling confirmation.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — [P1 confidence=100] `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&` When a team administrator who is not also the owner tries to manage a team booking, this conjunction makes `isTeamAdminOrOwner` false and the mutation rejects the supported administrator role as forbidden.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — [P1 confidence=100] `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email) &&` When the request repeats the same new address, every copy passes this pre-update attendee check and `createMany` inserts duplicate attendee records into the booking and calendar payload.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — [P1 confidence=100] `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` When a caller changes the case of an address present in the lowercased `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` configuration, this case-sensitive comparison admits and invites the blocked guest.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525 — [P1 confidence=100] `export const sendAddGuestsEmails = async (calEvent: CalendarEvent, newGuests: string[]) => {` When `disableStandardEmails.all.host` or `disableStandardEmails.all.attendee` is enabled for the event type, this notification path receives no metadata and sends the corresponding guest-change emails despite the configured suppression flag.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:147 — [P2 confidence=100] `};` When guests are added to a team booking, the constructed `CalendarEvent` closes without a `team` value, so the explicit `calendarEvent.team?.members` notification branch can never notify the booking's other assigned hosts.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — [P2 confidence=100] `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` When a request contains one already-attending address alongside one genuinely new address, passing the unfiltered input classifies the existing attendee as newly added and sends that person a fresh scheduled-confirmation email instead of the guest-change notification.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/_router.tsx:79 — [P2 confidence=100] `addGuests: authedProcedure.input(ZAddGuestsInputSchema).mutation(async ({ input, ctx }) => {` When authorization, deduplication, calendar propagation, or notification behavior regresses, this new mutation has no added automated test to fail CI, so the guest-management acceptance paths remain unverified.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — [P1 confidence=100] `const bookingAttendees = await prisma.booking.update({` For a single-guest request, any rejection from the later calendar update at line 165 occurs after this database write commits, so the caller receives failure while the guest remains stored and a retry is rejected as already present.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:531 — [P2 confidence=100] `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) {` For every team booking processed through addGuests.handler.ts, the constructed evt has no team property, so this branch is unreachable and no team member receives the new-guest email.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — [P2 confidence=100] `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` When the input contains both an existing attendee and a new guest, passing the pre-filter input causes email-manager.ts:541 to classify the existing attendee as new and send that attendee a duplicate scheduling confirmation.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:55 — [P3 confidence=100] `throw new TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN", message: "you_do_not_have_permission" });` When this permission path executes, the absent common.json key makes AddGuestsDialog render the literal `FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission` instead of a translated error.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — [P1 confidence=100] `const bookingAttendees = await prisma.booking.update({` When the later calendar-provider update rejects, the attendee insertion remains committed while the mutation reports failure, and retrying the same guest is rejected as already present instead of repairing the external event.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:170 — [P1 confidence=100] `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails");` When any organizer or attendee email send rejects, this catch discards the failure and line 173 returns success, so the UI confirms completion while at least one notification was dropped.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — [P1 confidence=100] `guests: z.array(z.string().email()),` A single request can supply an arbitrarily large guest array that is inserted, translated, propagated to a calendar provider, and expanded into concurrent email sends, creating unbounded request-path work and outbound amplification.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — [P1 confidence=100] `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter(` When the request repeats a new address, every copy survives this filter against the old attendee snapshot and reaches `createMany`, producing duplicate attendee work or an unhandled database constraint failure instead of a controlled 4xx.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:549 — [P2 confidence=100] `await Promise.all(emailsToSend);` This works for small bookings but breaks when attendee counts grow because it starts one email operation per organizer, team member, and attendee simultaneously, exhausting transporter or provider concurrency limits while awaiting the aggregate provides no cap.

packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:25 — [P2 confidence=100] `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)],` This works for small bookings but breaks as attendees accumulate because the unbounded Reply-To header eventually exceeds mail-provider or message-size limits, dropping the organizer notification while including every attendee is not a delivery cap.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:40 — [P2 confidence=75] `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate();` When cache invalidation rejects or outlives the success callback, the dialog closes and the mutation lifecycle reports success without awaiting or surfacing the refresh failure, leaving the booking list stale.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — [P2 confidence=75] `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&` Requiring a team user to be both admin and owner under-scopes the guest-management role set, so a non-owner team admin is forbidden from managing guests on the team booking.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:54 — [P1 confidence=75] `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) {` Treating attendee membership as mutation authority expands guest management beyond booking managers, so any authenticated attendee with the booking ID can add arbitrary recipients and trigger calendar updates and notification emails.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:54 — [P1 confidence=100] `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) {` Any authenticated attendee who submits the booking ID passes this authorization gate and can add arbitrary recipients to a booking they do not own, causing its title, description, location, attendee list, and video-call credentials to be disclosed in calendar invitations.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — [P1 confidence=100] `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` Changing the letter case of an address configured in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` bypasses this comparison because only the configured values are lowercased, so a prohibited recipient is added and invited.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — [P1 confidence=100] `guests: z.array(z.string().email()),` An authorized caller can submit an unbounded array containing the same new address repeatedly, causing duplicate attendee rows and one scheduled-email send per duplicate and thereby turning the endpoint into an email-bombing and resource-exhaustion primitive.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in addGuests.handler.ts line 158, credentials are fetched using `ctx.user` (the caller) rather than the booking owner. The code at lines 46-50 explicitly allows attendees and team admins to call this mutation for bookings they don't own. When they do, `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` gets the caller's credentials, not the booking owner's. The EventManager then uses these wrong credentials to call `updateCalendarAttendees`, which would fail to update the actual organizer's calendar or update the wrong calendar entirely. This is a real bug where the calendar integration credentials don't match the booking owner.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a transactional consistency issue. Looking at the diff in addGuests.handler.ts, the code first updates the database at line 92 with `prisma.booking.update()` to add guests, then later calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` at line 161. If the calendar update fails, the database already has the guests committed. The `uniqueGuests` filter at lines 68-72 checks `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`, so on retry, those guests would be filtered out as duplicates, preventing repair of the external calendar. This is a real consistency bug where partial failure leaves the system in an inconsistent state.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. The diff shows ZAddGuestsInputSchema with `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` which has no length limit. In addGuests.handler.ts, the code creates database records for all guests (createMany), builds translation promises for each attendee, calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, and sendAddGuestsEmails which creates one email promise per attendee via Promise.all. A malicious caller could submit thousands of email addresses in a single mutation, causing unbounded database inserts, translation lookups, calendar API calls, and concurrent email sends. This is a legitimate review concern for new nontrivial functionality - the diff shows complex authorization logic (isTeamAdminOrOwner, isOrganizer, isAttendee checks), guest deduplication against blacklist and existing attendees, calendar event updates via EventManager, and email notifications. The absence of tests for this new feature is a valid, specific, diff-grounded concern, not a generic 'add more tests' comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — [P1 confidence=100] `const bookingAttendees = await prisma.booking.update({` For a single-guest request, any rejection from the later calendar update at line 165 occurs after this database write commits, so the caller receives failure while the guest remains stored and a retry is rejected as already present.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a transactional consistency issue in addGuests.handler.ts. Looking at the diff, line 92-109 shows `prisma.booking.update()` that adds guests to the database, and line 165 shows `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` which can fail. If the calendar update fails after the database write succeeds, the guests are persisted in the database but the caller receives an error. A retry would fail because the guests are already present (filtered out by uniqueGuests check at line 73-76). This is a real atomicity/consistency bug where partial state can occur.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:531 — [P2 confidence=100] `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) {` For every team booking processed through addGuests.handler.ts, the constructed evt has no team property, so this branch is unreachable and no team member receives the new-guest email.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at addGuests.handler.ts, the evt CalendarEvent object is constructed without a 'team' property. The code builds evt with title, type, description, startTime, endTime, organizer, attendees, uid, recurringEvent, location, destinationCalendar, seatsPerTimeSlot, and seatsShowAttendees - but no 'team' field. In sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts:531), the code checks `if (calendarEvent.team?.members)` to send emails to team members, but since evt.team is never set in the handler, this condition will always be false and team members won't receive the new-guest notification email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — [P2 confidence=100] `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` When the input contains both an existing attendee and a new guest, passing the pre-filter input causes email-manager.ts:541 to classify the existing attendee as new and send that attendee a duplicate scheduling confirmation.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. In addGuests.handler.ts line 168, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the original `guests` input array, not `uniqueGuests` which was filtered to remove existing attendees. Looking at email-manager.ts lines 533-540, the code checks `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide whether to send AttendeeScheduledEmail (for new guests) or AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (for existing attendees). If `guests` contains an email that's already an attendee (which was filtered out by `uniqueGuests` but still exists in the original `guests` array), that existing attendee would incorrectly receive AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. The fix should be to pass `uniqueGuests` instead of `guests`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:55 — [P3 confidence=100] `throw new TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN", message: "you_do_not_have_permission" });` When this permission path executes, the absent common.json key makes AddGuestsDialog render the literal `FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission` instead of a translated error.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the error message 'you_do_not_have_permission' is used in addGuests.handler.ts line 55, but looking at the common.json diff, this translation key is not added. The diff shows new keys like 'guests_added', 'unable_to_add_guests', 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' being added, but 'you_do_not_have_permission' is not among them. The error handler in AddGuestsDialog.tsx formats the error as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, so if the key doesn't exist, it would show the literal untranslated string. This is a real bug - a missing i18n key for an error that can occur.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — [P1 confidence=100] `const bookingAttendees = await prisma.booking.update({` When the later calendar-provider update rejects, the attendee insertion remains committed while the mutation reports failure, and retrying the same guest is rejected as already present instead of repairing the external event.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a transactional consistency issue in the addGuests.handler.ts. Looking at the diff, the handler first updates the database with `prisma.booking.update()` at line 92 to add attendees, then later calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` at line 155. If the calendar update fails, the database changes are already committed (no transaction wrapper), leaving the system in an inconsistent state where attendees exist in the database but not in the external calendar. Retrying would fail because the guests are already in the database. This is a real correctness/data consistency bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:170 — [P1 confidence=100] `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails");` When any organizer or attendee email send rejects, this catch discards the failure and line 173 returns success, so the UI confirms completion while at least one notification was dropped.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at lines 169-173 in addGuests.handler.ts that when sendAddGuestsEmails fails, the error is caught and only logged with console.log, then the function continues to return { message: 'Guests added' } at line 174. This means the API returns success even when email notifications fail to send, which is a silent failure that could leave users unaware that notifications weren't delivered. The finding accurately describes this behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — [P1 confidence=100] `guests: z.array(z.string().email()),` A single request can supply an arbitrarily large guest array that is inserted, translated, propagated to a calendar provider, and expanded into concurrent email sends, creating unbounded request-path work and outbound amplification.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` in the schema with no size limit. The handler in addGuests.handler.ts processes all guests: creates database records for each (`createMany`), builds attendee lists with translations for each, calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, and sends emails to all guests via `sendAddGuestsEmails`. This creates unbounded work proportional to array size - a single request with thousands of emails would cause database inserts, translation lookups, calendar API calls, and email sends for each. This is a real denial-of-service/resource exhaustion vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — [P1 confidence=100] `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter(` When the request repeats a new address, every copy survives this filter against the old attendee snapshot and reaches `createMany`, producing duplicate attendee work or an unhandled database constraint failure instead of a controlled 4xx.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the uniqueGuests filter at line 74 only checks against `booking.attendees` (the existing attendees from the database snapshot). If the `guests` input array contains duplicate emails (e.g., ['a@b.com', 'a@b.com']), both copies pass the filter since neither is in the original attendees list. These duplicates then reach `createMany` at line 91, which would either create duplicate attendee records or fail with a database constraint error depending on the schema. The code lacks deduplication of the input array itself before filtering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:549 — [P2 confidence=100] `await Promise.all(emailsToSend);` This works for small bookings but breaks when attendee counts grow because it starts one email operation per organizer, team member, and attendee simultaneously, exhausting transporter or provider concurrency limits while awaiting the aggregate provides no cap.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that sendAddGuestsEmails uses Promise.all to send emails to all organizers, team members, and attendees simultaneously without any concurrency limiting. This is a real pattern in the diff (lines 522-541 in email-manager.ts). However, this is not a bug per se - it's an architectural concern about scalability. The same pattern exists in the adjacent sendLocationChangeEmails function, suggesting this is the established pattern in the codebase. While the concern about exhausting provider limits at scale is valid, it's more of a scalability/architecture consideration than a defect that would cause immediate breakage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:25 — [P2 confidence=100] `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)],` This works for small bookings but breaks as attendees accumulate because the unbounded Reply-To header eventually exceeds mail-provider or message-size limits, dropping the organizer notification while including every attendee is not a delivery cap.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that including all attendees in the Reply-To header will 'break' due to mail-provider or message-size limits. However, this is speculative - there's no evidence in the diff that this is a real problem. The pattern of including attendees in Reply-To is common in email systems and used elsewhere in the codebase (similar patterns exist in other email templates). The claim about 'unbounded' headers causing delivery failures is theoretical and not a verifiable defect from this diff. Additionally, the confidence level of 100% is inappropriate for such a speculative concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:40 — [P2 confidence=75] `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate();` When cache invalidation rejects or outlives the success callback, the dialog closes and the mutation lifecycle reports success without awaiting or surfacing the refresh failure, leaving the booking list stale.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that if cache invalidation fails, the dialog closes and reports success without surfacing the error. However, looking at the code, `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` is called in the `onSuccess` callback after `showToast(t('guests_added'), 'success')`. The invalidate() call is a fire-and-forget cache invalidation - this is standard tRPC/React Query pattern. If invalidation fails, the mutation itself already succeeded (guests were added to the database). The UI showing success is correct because the actual operation succeeded. Cache invalidation failure is a minor UX issue at worst (stale data until refresh), not a bug. This is standard React Query usage and not a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — [P2 confidence=75] `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&` Requiring a team user to be both admin and owner under-scopes the guest-management role set, so a non-owner team admin is forbidden from managing guests on the team booking.

adjudication.rationale: The code at line 47 uses `&&` (AND) between `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`, meaning a user must be BOTH admin AND owner to pass this check. This is likely a bug - it should probably be `||` (OR) to allow either team admins OR team owners to manage guests. As written, a team admin who is not also an owner would be incorrectly forbidden from adding guests to team bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:54 — [P1 confidence=75] `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) {` Treating attendee membership as mutation authority expands guest management beyond booking managers, so any authenticated attendee with the booking ID can add arbitrary recipients and trigger calendar updates and notification emails.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a security concern in the authorization logic. The code at line 54 allows any attendee (isAttendee) to add guests to a booking, not just organizers or team admins. This means any existing attendee can add arbitrary email addresses as guests, triggering calendar updates and notification emails. This is a permissive authorization model that may not be intentional - typically only organizers should be able to modify booking attendees. The diff clearly shows this logic: `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` throws FORBIDDEN, meaning attendees pass the check and can add guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:54 — [P1 confidence=100] `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) {` Any authenticated attendee who submits the booking ID passes this authorization gate and can add arbitrary recipients to a booking they do not own, causing its title, description, location, attendee list, and video-call credentials to be disclosed in calendar invitations.

adjudication.rationale: The authorization check at line 54 allows any authenticated user who is an attendee of the booking to add guests. The code checks `isAttendee` by matching `user.email` against `booking.attendees`, meaning any existing attendee can add arbitrary new guests to the booking. This causes the booking details (title, description, location, attendee list, video call credentials) to be disclosed to the new guests via calendar invitations and emails. This is a security/authorization bug - attendees should typically not have permission to add other guests to a booking they don't own, as this could lead to information disclosure to unauthorized parties.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — [P1 confidence=100] `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` Changing the letter case of an address configured in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` bypasses this comparison because only the configured values are lowercased, so a prohibited recipient is added and invited.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at lines 68-77 in addGuests.handler.ts, the blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased via `.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`, but the `guest` variable being compared via `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` is NOT lowercased. This means if BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS contains 'bad@example.com', a user could bypass the check by submitting 'BAD@example.com' or 'Bad@Example.com'. This is a real security bypass bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — [P1 confidence=100] `guests: z.array(z.string().email()),` An authorized caller can submit an unbounded array containing the same new address repeatedly, causing duplicate attendee rows and one scheduled-email send per duplicate and thereby turning the endpoint into an email-bombing and resource-exhaustion primitive.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real security issue. Looking at the diff: 1) The schema in addGuests.schema.ts only validates that guests is an array of email strings with no uniqueness constraint or size limit. 2) In addGuests.handler.ts, the uniqueGuests filter only removes emails that already exist in booking.attendees, but does NOT deduplicate within the input array itself. 3) The handler then creates attendee records for all items in uniqueGuests and sends emails via sendAddGuestsEmails. If a caller submits the same new email address multiple times in the guests array, each duplicate would pass the uniqueGuests filter (since it checks against existing attendees, not against other items in the input), creating duplicate attendee rows and triggering multiple email sends. This is a valid resource exhaustion and email bombing vulnerability.
